evidence_items.source_quote: A 3-year-old neutered domestic shorthair cat was referred for a nodular dermatitis that had appeared 2 months previously.

rationale: A 3-year-old neutered domestic shorthair cat presenting with multifocal cutaneous phaeohyphomycosis caused by Exophiala spinifera. Cryptococcosis was considered only on the differential diagnosis list. The patient is non-human (feline) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: A man with recently diagnosed HIV and cryptococcal meningitis had been started on ART one month prior to this (see Table 1 for more information).

rationale: A male HIV patient evaluated for severe illness and diagnosed with disseminated Mycobacterium avium and tuberculous meningitis based on positive urine AlereLAM. Cryptococcal meningitis is mentioned solely as a prior historical diagnosis from one month before presentation without active evaluation or confirmatory diagnostic evidence during the current clinical episode -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A six-year-old female boxer dog presented with a 13-month history of progressive and mildly pruritic skin lesions.

rationale: A 6-year-old female boxer dog diagnosed with cutaneous protothecosis (Prototheca wickerhamii). Cryptococcosis was mentioned solely in the context of an amphotericin B dosing protocol borrowed from canine cryptococcosis. The subject is non-human (canine) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: An intact female 8-week-old domestic shorthair cat was taken into a foster/rescue home and cohabited a house with approximately nine other cats.

rationale: An intact female 8-week-old domestic shorthair cat evaluated for progressive neurological signs diagnosed with feline infectious peritonitis. Cryptococcus antibody titers were tested and negative. Subject is non-human (feline) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cutaneous cryptococcosis was diagnosed in four male patients seen during dermatological interconsultations of a tertiary hospital, with a mean age of 41 years.

rationale: This case record unit describes an aggregate cohort of four patients presenting with cutaneous cryptococcosis seen during dermatological consultations ('Cutaneous cryptococcosis was diagnosed in four male patients seen during dermatological interconsultations of a tertiary hospital, with a mean age of 41 years.'). Because it represents an aggregate multi-patient cohort unit without a single separable patient anchor, it is excluded -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

evidence_items.source_quote: A biopsy was taken from the lesions of the patients, and histopathology confirmed the diagnosis of cryptococcosis in all cases (Figure 3). Cultures of the biopsy specimens were positive for Cryptococcus in three cases and negative in one.
evidence_items.test_name: Biopsy histopathology and culture across cohort

rationale: This case record unit reports aggregate clinical examination, biopsy histopathology, and culture findings across four patients ('A biopsy was taken from the lesions of the patients, and histopathology confirmed the diagnosis of cryptococcosis in all cases (Figure 3). Cultures of the biopsy specimens were positive for Cryptococcus in three cases and negative in one.'). As a multi-patient aggregate description rather than a single-patient clinical episode, it is excluded -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

evidence_items.source_quote: Treatment was started with amphotericin B and fluconazole for patients 1, 2 and 3 for two weeks, then maintenance therapy with fluconazole alone.

rationale: This unit details aggregate treatment regimens across a group of four patients ('Treatment was started with amphotericin B and fluconazole for patients 1, 2 and 3 for two weeks, then maintenance therapy with fluconazole alone. Patient 4 received amphotericin B and flucytosine for two weeks...'). It is an aggregate multi-subject unit rather than an individual single-patient clinical episode -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

evidence_items.source_quote: An 18-month-old male neutered Ragdoll was referred to Veterinary Specialist Services, Underwood, Queensland, Australia, with an 8 week history of progressive unilateral right-sided mucopurulent nasal discharge and exophthalmos (right eye; OD).

rationale: An 18-month-old male neutered Ragdoll cat evaluated for unilateral exophthalmos and retrobulbar abscess. Serological testing for Cryptococcus antigen was negative. Because the patient is a non-human animal (feline), this case is excluded from human clinical benchmarking -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: A forty-two-year-old female PLHIV (people living with HIV) not on antiretroviral treatment (ART) was admitted with the history of sudden onset left hemiplegia and altered sensorium for 4 days.
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical presentation of brain abscess patient
evidence_items.target_concept: Cryptococcosis not evaluated / non-target MAI abscess

rationale: A 42-year-old female with HIV presenting with left hemiplegia and altered sensorium, diagnosed with a right frontoparietal brain abscess due to non-tuberculous mycobacteria (Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare / MAI). The segmented case narrative contains no mention of the target disease Cryptococcosis or any diagnostic testing for Cryptococcus. Excluded under target case criteria -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A duodenal histoplasmosis and cryptococcosis infection were treated from June 2012 with a 3-week course of amphotericin B - flucytosine followed by oral voriconazole 100 mg bid.

rationale: A 35-year-old female with AIDS presenting for therapeutic drug monitoring and pharmacogenetic management of voriconazole clearance influenced by CYP2C19 polymorphisms and ART interactions, who ultimately died of PML. Cryptococcosis is cited only as a remote past medical history indication from June 2012 for prior antifungal therapy without any active diagnostic workup or confirmatory clinical evidence during the presented episode -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A 7-year-old spayed domestic longhair cat was presented to Murdoch University Veterinary Hospital for evaluation of left head tilt, dysphonia, head shaking, inappetance and weight loss of 2 weeks' duration.

rationale: A 7-year-old spayed domestic longhair cat presenting with an aural mass and skull base erosion confirmed to have Cryptococcus gattii infection. The subject is non-human (feline) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: A 12-year-old, 12 kg, spayed, female terrier mix was noted by her owner to have excess tearing and a collection of blood in her left eye.

rationale: A 12-year-old female terrier mix dog evaluated for uveitis and hyphema diagnosed with metastatic splenic hemangiosarcoma; fungal serology for cryptococcus was negative. The subject is non-human (canine) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: An 8-year-old tortoiseshell spayed female domestic shorthair cat was referred for anorexia, weight loss and progressive trismus of at least 1 month duration.

rationale: An 8-year-old tortoiseshell spayed female domestic shorthair cat presented with progressive trismus, anorexia, and purulent nasal discharge. Computed tomography and masticatory muscle biopsies revealed fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP)-like disease. Infectious disease screening including Cryptococcus species serology was negative. The patient is non-human (feline veterinary subject) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient, who was a woman in her early 70s with an unremarkable previous medical history, except for 2-year follow-up against lung cryptococcosis and traffic accident, incidentally presented with unenhanced and low-density, heterogeneous and increasing mass on abdominal dynamic computed tomography (CT) in the peripheral right lobe of the liver

rationale: A woman in her early 70s presenting with an incidental hepatic mass detected during follow-up, diagnosed with primary hepatic inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor (IMT) after surgical resection and immunohistochemistry. Lung cryptococcosis is mentioned only as a prior 2-year past medical history without active clinical illness, evaluation, or confirmatory testing during this surgical episode -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: An 11-year-old spayed female cat presented with a 6-month history of a progressive skin disease consisting of asymmetric eroded nodules on the head, right paw pad, shoulder and caudal dorsum.

rationale: An 11-year-old spayed female cat presenting with progressive skin nodules, ocular lesions, vomiting, and weight loss, diagnosed with cutaneous nodular and ocular Cryptococcus neoformans based on cytology, histopathology, serum CrAg titer >1:524288, and PCR/fungal culture. The patient is non-human (feline veterinary subject) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: Six months prior to this presentation he had been diagnosed with cryptococcal meningitis. His initial treatment consisted of amphotericin B and flucytosine, after which he was maintained on chronic suppressive fluconazole therapy.

rationale: A 58-year-old male heart transplant recipient presenting with acute heart rejection and inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (IDP) responsive to plasmapheresis and steroids. Cryptococcal meningitis is mentioned purely as past medical history diagnosed 6 months prior, which had led to reduction in immunosuppressive regimen, without active infection or diagnostic evaluation in the current episode -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A 28-year-old patient had Cryptococcus neoformans infection and disseminated visceral leishmaniasis, the only case described to date.

rationale: A 4-year-old male with a STAT1 gain-of-function mutation presenting with severe visceral leishmaniasis and hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Cryptococcus neoformans is mentioned solely in the discussion citing literature from a separate study (Dotta et al.) involving an unrelated 28-year-old patient. The subject in this case report did not have cryptococcosis -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A 9-year-old female spayed indoor-only American Domestic Shorthair cat (3.72 kg, 8.20 lb) was presented for progressive ill-defined pain, malaise, in appetence, and reluctance to jump.
evidence_items.test_name: Veterinary clinical evaluation / Cryptococcus antigen titer

rationale: A 9-year-old female spayed American Domestic Shorthair cat presenting with neck pain and malaise. Infectious disease testing included negative Cryptococcus antigen titer. Subject is non-human (feline) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: Prior opportunistic infections included oral candidiasis and cryptococcal meningitis.

rationale: A 57-year-old male with untreated HIV presenting with cough and dyspnea, diagnosed with acute Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia on transbronchial biopsy. Cryptococcal meningitis is mentioned solely as a remote prior opportunistic infection in the past medical history from 20 years earlier without active investigation or relevance during the current episode -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: meningitis caused by Cryptococcus neoformans at the age of 7 years (Table 1).

rationale: A 13-year-old male evaluated at an immunology clinic for recurrent infections and diagnosed with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID). Meningitis caused by Cryptococcus neoformans is mentioned solely as a past medical history event that occurred at age 7 years without active infection during the current clinical episode -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Complicating her immunosuppression, Cryptococcus neoformans meningitis was diagnosed through lumbar puncture seven months earlier.

rationale: An 18-year-old female with lupus nephritis on hemodialysis presenting with a catheter-associated right atrial thrombus and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia bacteremia. Cryptococcus neoformans meningitis was diagnosed 7 months earlier on maintenance fluconazole, and is cited only as a pre-existing historical condition without active cryptococcal disease in this encounter -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: In our review of 164 cases, we found 89 (52%) had skin manifestations.

rationale: A comprehensive narrative review and cohort synthesis discussing immunopathology and infectious complications (including Cryptococcus) in 164 cases of idiopathic CD4+ lymphocytopenia. Does not describe an individual patient case report -> EXCLUDED_NON_CASE_REPORT.

evidence_items.source_quote: Considerations included leptomeningeal disease from metastatic carcinoma or lymphoma as well as PCNSL due to the patient's age and multifocal nature of her symptoms, as well as tuberculosis, histoplasmosis, coccidioidomycosis, or cryptococcosis, and sarcoidosis.

rationale: A 70-year-old woman presenting with left arm weakness, numbness, and cranial nerve III palsy. Cranial MRI demonstrated suprasellar and right periatrial enhancing lesions. Differential diagnosis included metastatic lymphoma, PCNSL, tuberculosis, histoplasmosis, coccidioidomycosis, cryptococcosis, and sarcoidosis. Stereotactic biopsy of the periatrial lesion confirmed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Cryptococcosis was only considered as a differential diagnosis without specific diagnostic workup -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: She has past histories of glaucoma and pulmonary cryptococcosis.

rationale: A 63-year-old female diagnosed with adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATL) who underwent allogeneic peripheral blood stem cell transplantation and subsequently developed paraplegia due to HTLV-I-associated myelopathy/CNS relapse. Pulmonary cryptococcosis was noted purely as a remote past medical history without current manifestation or workup -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Seven branch-specific reactions (A-G) for the detection of common moulds (Aspergillus, Penicillium (A), Rhizopus, Mucor, Rhizomucor (B), Absidia, Lichtheimia, Cunninghamella (C), Fusarium and Scedosporium (D) and yeasts (Cryptococcus (E), Trichosporon (F) and Candida (G)) using a branch-specific primer targeting the nuclear ribosomal internal transcribed spacer 2 (ITS) region and a universal primer targeting the 28S RNA-encoding region.

rationale: A patient in their early twenties with classical Hodgkin lymphoma who died of disseminated Trichosporon asahii fungemia. In a retrospective study evaluating an experimental broad-range fungal PCR array on blood samples, reaction E was designed to detect Cryptococcus spp. Cryptococcosis was not suspected or diagnosed in the patient, appearing solely as a methodology component of the fungal PCR assay -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step4_condition_matched: Cryptococcus neoformans antibody testing in dog

evidence_items.source_quote: A 10-year-old male, neutered [18.8 kg (41.36 lb)] mixed breed dog was referred for evaluation of a 9-day history of cervical hyperesthesia.

rationale: A 10-year-old neutered male mixed breed dog presenting with cervical hyperesthesia and vertebral venous sinus thrombosis. Cryptococcus neoformans antibody testing was performed as part of infectious workup. The subject is non-human (canine) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: infections manifesting with visceral enlarged lymph nodes are more frequently due to intracellular microscopically or microbiologically easy to identify agents (i.e. Cryptococcus, mycobacteria)

rationale: A 50-year-old HIV-positive male evaluated for visceral PET-positive lymph nodes and diagnosed with visceral leishmaniasis based on histiocytes laden with amastigotes. Cryptococcus is mentioned solely as a background/literature example of intracellular agents causing enlarged visceral lymph nodes without active clinical diagnosis -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: fungal infections (including candidiasis, mucormycosis, cryptococcosis, histoplasmosis, and paracoccidioidomycosis);

rationale: A 49-year-old male presenting with dyspnea and a pulmonary halo sign, diagnosed by histopathology with lung adenocarcinoma with a lepidic growth pattern. Cryptococcosis is mentioned strictly as an entry in a general textbook differential diagnosis list for the CT halo sign -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: We searched the PubMed database using the keywords "biliary", "cryptococcus", and "biliary cryptococcosis".

rationale: A literature review analyzing 11 previously published cases of biliary cryptococcosis identified from a PubMed search. The text summarizes aggregate demographic, clinical, diagnostic, and therapeutic findings rather than presenting an individual clinical case report -> EXCLUDED_NON_CASE_REPORT.

evidence_items.source_quote: At age 15 years, she developed severe headache, neck stiffness, photophobia, wide-based gait, and microzoopsia. She was diagnosed with cryptococcal meningoencephalitis and successfully treated with daily liposomal amphotericin B for 4 weeks and flucytosine for 2 weeks, followed by 10 weeks of fluconazole at a therapeutic dosage, later continued at a prophylactic dosage.

rationale: A 3-year-old female followed into adolescence for congenital anemia and diagnosed with Cartilage-Hair Hypoplasia (CHH) treated with HSCT. Cryptococcal meningoencephalitis is mentioned as a historical past infection at age 15 years without current presentation or primary laboratory test results in the narrative -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Infectious disease testing submitted on day 1 included feline leukemia virus and Cryptococcus antigen testing, and feline immunodeficiency virus, coronavirus, Toxoplasma gondii and Bartonella henselae serologic testing through a commercial laboratory (Antech New York laboratory) and were negative.
evidence_items.target_concept: Cryptococcus antigen differential in feline patient

rationale: A 3-year-old spayed female domestic shorthair cat presenting with cluster seizures and hyperthermia. Infectious disease evaluation included Cryptococcus antigen testing, which was negative, and the cat was ultimately diagnosed with a drug reaction to phenobarbital. Because the patient is a non-human veterinary subject (feline), this case is excluded -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: A total of 24 patients with non-TBM who were admitted to our Department of Neurology from January 2017 to June 2021 and diagnosed with early cerebrospinal fluid changes consistent with the characteristics of TBM were selected.

rationale: This publication describes an aggregate clinical study cohort of 24 non-TBM neurological patients ('A total of 24 patients with non-TBM who were admitted to our Department of Neurology from January 2017 to June 2021...'), including 5 cases of cryptococcal meningitis, analyzed collectively for CSF metagenomic NGS diagnostic performance. As an aggregate cohort study unit rather than a single individual patient case report, it is excluded -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

evidence_items.source_quote: During the study period, six patients were included. Clinical, epidemiological, and fungal characteristics are reported in  Table 1 .
evidence_items.test_name: Multi-patient study design / case series description

rationale: This report describes an aggregate case series of six immunocompetent patients diagnosed with cryptococcal meningoencephalitis and cryptococcoma in French Guiana ('During the study period, six patients were included. Clinical, epidemiological, and fungal characteristics are reported in Table 1...'). Because this is an aggregate multi-patient case series rather than an individual patient case report, it is excluded -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

evidence_items.source_quote: A precautionary Cryptococcus antigen latex test was performed owing to the new nasal lesion but was negative.

rationale: A 6-year-old neutered male domestic shorthair cat presenting with pruritic, non-healing cutaneous lesions diagnosed with feline leishmaniosis. A precautionary Cryptococcus antigen latex test was performed and negative. The subject is non-human (feline) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: Negative infectious tests were obtained 14 days later (Tick panel PCR, serology for Neospora antibodies, and Cryptococcus antigen latex).

rationale: A 3-year-old female Australian Shepherd dog evaluated for progressive left head tilt and meningoencephalitis. Infectious disease workup including Cryptococcus antigen latex testing was negative. Veterinary non-human patient -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: Evidence for optic nerve infiltration by C. neoformans has come from case reports only.

rationale: This document excerpt represents an academic narrative review and discussion section discussing mechanisms of cryptococcal optic neuropathy and citing prior literature case reports (Lipson et al., Ofner, Cohen et al., Corti et al.), rather than an individual primary clinical case report -> EXCLUDED_NON_CASE_REPORT.

evidence_items.source_quote: A 9-year-old, non-ambulatory intact male Shih Tzu dog presented to our clinic 1 day after the peracute onset of neurological signs.

rationale: A 9-year-old intact male Shih Tzu dog presenting with acute onset of non-ambulatory tetraparesis diagnosed with fibrocartilaginous embolism on diffusion-weighted MRI and postmortem histopathology. Cryptococcus is mentioned only in the differential discussion for spinal disease in veterinary medicine. Non-human veterinary patient -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: A 2-year-old, 2.5 kg spayed female domestic shorthair cat with a 1-year history of chronic sneezing and nasal discharge was presented for CT and rhinoscopy.

rationale: A 2-year-old spayed female domestic shorthair cat presenting with chronic sneezing and nasal discharge undergoing rhinoscopy complicated by iatrogenic ocular trauma. Serum Cryptococcus antigen testing was performed as part of feline chronic rhinitis workup. Non-human veterinary patient -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: Cultures of ganglion aspirate were negative for bacteria, acid-fast bacilli, and fungi. Histopathology of cervical lymph nodes was negative for intracellular microbes.
evidence_items.test_name: Ganglion aspirate culture and cervical lymph node histopathology
evidence_items.specimen: ganglion aspirate and cervical lymph nodes

rationale: A pediatric male with inherited IL-12Rβ1 deficiency presenting with regional suppurative adenitis, polyserositis, and abscesses, diagnosed with Salmonella choleraesuis bacteremia and BCG regional adenitis. Lymph node and ganglion aspirate cultures were negative for fungi, and cryptococcosis was neither diagnosed nor specifically suspected in this patient; it is cited only as general background in the broader literature regarding the infectious spectrum of IL-12Rβ1 deficiency -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serological tests for feline immunodeficiency virus antibody, feline leukemia virus antigen (SNAP FIV/FeLV Combo Test; IDEXX Laboratories) and Cryptococcus antigen (Remel Cryptococcus Antigen Latex Test; Thermo Fisher Scientific) were negative.

rationale: A 1.5-year-old neutered domestic shorthair cat presenting with progressive nasal swelling and hyporexia diagnosed with nasal phaeohyphomycosis caused by a novel Cladophialophora species. Serological testing for Cryptococcus antigen was negative. Because the patient is a non-human animal (feline), the case is excluded from human clinical benchmarks -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: CSF studies were negative for infection.
evidence_items.target_concept: Infection ruled out in VP shunt evaluation

rationale: A 32-year-old male presenting with headache and abdominal discomfort due to an abdominal pseudocyst complicating a ventriculoperitoneal shunt originally placed in infancy. Lumbar puncture demonstrated elevated opening pressure but CSF studies were negative for infection, and pseudocyst cultures were negative. The target condition Cryptococcosis is not present, diagnosed, or investigated in this patient's clinical episode; the candidate pair was generated solely because another unrelated case report in the same multi-case publication involved cryptococcal meningitis -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A 40-year-old male with a history human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)/acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) and hydrocephalus secondary to cryptococcal meningitis presented to the emergency room with diffuse abdominal pain and three episodes of nausea and vomiting.

rationale: A 40-year-old male with HIV/AIDS and hydrocephalus secondary to remote cryptococcal meningitis presenting with acute abdominal pain and pseudocyst complicating his ventriculoperitoneal shunt. Pseudocyst fluid grew Streptococcus Group D. Cryptococcal meningitis is cited strictly as remote past medical history explaining the etiology of his ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement, with no active cryptococcosis or antifungal treatment during the current care episode -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

step4_condition_matched: Cryptococcus antigen latex test in feline patient

evidence_items.source_quote: An estimated 7-year-old 6.1-kg male castrated domestic shorthair cat presented to a local emergency clinic for head pressing.
A cryptococcus antigen latex test was negative.

rationale: An estimated 7-year-old male castrated domestic shorthair cat presenting with neurological signs (head pressing) diagnosed with intracranial blastomycosis. Blood was submitted for cryptococcosis testing and a cryptococcus antigen latex test was negative. Because the patient is a non-human animal (feline), this case is excluded -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: Unfortunately, 2 months later the patient died of complications (cryptococcal meningitis, hydrocephalus and ischemic stroke).

rationale: A 58-year-old female with advanced chronic lymphocytic leukemia and MALT lymphoma studied for clonal evolution using single-cell RNA sequencing. Cryptococcal meningitis is mentioned purely in passing as a fatal terminal complication occurring months after meningioma resection ('Unfortunately, 2 months later the patient died of complications (cryptococcal meningitis, hydrocephalus and ischemic stroke)'), with no diagnostic evaluation, microbiological testing, CSF data, or treatment details described. Background mention of a terminal complication in a non-target study -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Testing for tuberculosis using sputum stained with auramine and cryptococcosis using cerebrospinal fluid stained with India ink was negative in all of them.

rationale: This case record unit describes an aggregate cohort of four women with HIV presenting with fever, cough, and skin lesions ('Four women with HIV but unknown CD4+ T-cell count were received...'). CSF India ink examination for cryptococcosis was performed and negative across the cohort. Because this is an aggregate multi-patient case series rather than a single individual patient episode, it is excluded -> EXCLUDED_NON_SINGLE_PATIENT.

evidence_items.source_quote: A 2-year-old neutered male domestic mixed-breed cat, weighing 1.8 kg, was admitted to a veterinary hospital after being rescued eight months prior.

rationale: A 2-year-old neutered male domestic mixed-breed cat evaluated for progressive respiratory and ocular disease diagnosed with feline panleukopenia and herpesvirus. Diagnostic DNA pathogen testing for Cryptococcus spp. was performed. The subject is non-human (feline) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: A 2.5-year-old female entire Pomeranian dog was presented to the neurology department of IVC Evidensia Small Animal Hospital (Arnhem, The Netherlands)

rationale: A 2.5-year-old female Pomeranian dog presenting with acute neurological deficits diagnosed with necrotizing leukomyelitis and meningitis. Diagnostic testing of brain tissue for Cryptococcus neoformans was negative. The subject is non-human (canine) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: In the case of Cryptococcus and MTB, positive mNGS results were considered when at least 1 unique read was mapped to species level

rationale: A case describing next-generation sequencing evaluation for diagnosis of a non-cryptococcal infection. Cryptococcus is mentioned only in the bioinformatics methods section describing diagnostic read threshold mapping -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Invasive fungal infections usually occur in immunocompromised hosts, with the most common pathogens in SLE patients being Candida albicans, Cryptococcus neoformans, and Aspergillus spp.

rationale: A 43-year-old female with SLE presenting with paracoccidioidomycosis discitis. Cryptococcus neoformans is mentioned solely as a background general comment regarding common fungal pathogens in SLE patients -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Fundus angiography showed vitreous opacity in the right eye and a hypofluorescence lesion with hyperfluorescence margin in the peripheral retinal region in the early stage (Fig. 2).

rationale: A middle-aged female presenting with visual decline in the right eye diagnosed with acute retinal necrosis. The provided text segment of the report ends after fundus angiography without presenting microbiological, lumbar puncture, or fungal diagnostic findings -> INCONCLUSIVE_DATA.

evidence_items.source_quote: For bacteria and fungi (Mycobacteria and Cryptococcus were excluded), a positive mNGS result was given when its coverage ranked among the top 10 of the same kind of microbes and was absent in the NTC

rationale: A case report of a 6-year-old child presenting with septic shock due to Fusobacterium necrophorum diagnosed via mNGS. Cryptococcus is mentioned solely within the general laboratory description of mNGS bioinformatics filtering thresholds and cutoffs, with no clinical suspicion, active testing, or diagnosis of cryptococcosis in the patient -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Mycobacterium genavense, Histoplasma, and Cryptococcus neoformans.

rationale: A 54-year-old male presenting with disseminated Rhodococcus equi infection. Cryptococcus neoformans is mentioned solely as a comparative histopathologic differential in the discussion section -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The patient was eventually discharged home and continued on oral fluconazole, with a plan to complete a minimum of 12 months of therapy, before commencing secondary prophylaxis given his ongoing immunosuppression.

rationale: A brief discharge summary fragment noting continuation of oral fluconazole secondary prophylaxis without microbiological or diagnostic details in the provided segment -> INCONCLUSIVE_DATA.

evidence_items.source_quote: For viruses, M. tuberculosis, and Cryptococcus, a positive mNGS result was considered when at least one unique read was mapped to species level

rationale: A 65-year-old female presenting with pulmonary actinomycosis diagnosed by mNGS. Cryptococcus is mentioned only in the bioinformatics methods defining read reporting thresholds -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Latex cryptococcal antigen titres (LCAT) were also analysed and were negative.

rationale: A 7-year-old neutered male Yorkshire terrier dog presenting with generalized tetanus. CSF latex cryptococcal antigen titres (LCAT) and PCR were negative. The subject is non-human (canine) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: castrated domestic shorthair cat was presented to the emergency service at the University of California Davis Veterinary Medical Teaching Hospital

rationale: An 8-year-old female spayed domestic shorthair cat presenting with severe upper respiratory tract signs diagnosed with feline herpesvirus-1. Cryptococcus antigen titer was negative. The subject is non-human (feline) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: Due to the atypical morphology, distinct from more commonly recognized fungal pathogens such as Cryptococcus and Blastomyces species, further diagnostics were pursued.

rationale: Veterinary case report evaluating two domestic cats with cutaneous phaeohyphomycosis caused by Exophiala spinifera. Cryptococcus was discussed as a differential morphological entity. The subjects are non-human (felines) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.

evidence_items.source_quote: His disease was refractory, and complications included Cushing's syndrome and disseminated cryptococcus.

rationale: An 81-year-old male presenting with penile urethral urothelial carcinoma complicating junctional epidermolysis bullosa. Disseminated cryptococcus is mentioned solely as a remote historical complication from high-dose corticosteroid management in adolescence over 60 years earlier, with no active clinical relevance or current episode evaluation -> EXCLUDED_NON_TARGET_CASE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Comprehensive whole blood polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing for infectious diseases, including feline calicivirus, Cytauxzoon felis, Bartonella spp., Anaplasma spp., Ehrlichia spp., feline coronavirus, Mycoplasma haemofelis, Candidatus Mycoplasma haemominutum, Candidatus Mycoplasma turicensis, FeLV, FIV, Cryptococcus spp., Salmonella spp., Toxoplasma gondii, and feline panleukopenia, later yielded negative results.

rationale: A 3.3-year-old castrated male domestic shorthair cat presenting laterally recumbent in a pool of urine with vocalization and lethargy. Comprehensive whole blood PCR testing for infectious diseases including Cryptococcus spp. was negative. The patient is non-human (feline) -> EXCLUDED_NON_HUMAN.
